title: nepeta sulphurea subsp. lydiae
intro: Nepeta sulphurea subsp. lydiae, commonly known as Turkish catmint, is a perennial flowering plant belonging to the mint family (Lamiaceae). The plant has been used in traditional medicine for its health benefits, including its anti-inflammatory and antiseptic properties, which can help to soothe digestive issues, reduce fever, and promote wound healing. The therapeutic actions of Turkish catmint include its ability to act as an antispasmodic, calming the nervous system and relieving cramps and spasms, as well as its antioxidant properties, which can help to protect against cell damage and oxidative stress. The bioactive constituents of Nepeta sulphurea subsp. lydiae include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and essential oils, such as nepetalactone, which are responsible for its medicinal properties.
